source.author: hor
source.text: saepius ventis agitatur ingens pinus et celsae graviore casu decidunt turres feriuntque summos fulgura montis sperat infestis, metuit secundis alteram sortem bene praeparatum pectus.
source.text_original: saepius ventis agitatur ingens / pinus et celsae graviore casu / decidunt turres feriuntque summos / fulgura montis / sperat infestis, metuit secundis / alteram sortem bene praeparatum / pectus.
source.text_english: The mighty pine is more often battered by winds, and towering towers fall with a heavier crash, and lightning strikes the mountain peaks; the heart that is well prepared hopes for a second fortune in adversity, and fears it in success.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: regum talis condicio est, feriuntque summos fulgura montes.
reuse.text_original: 'regum talis condicio est, feriuntque summos fulgura montes'.
reuse.text_english: Such is the condition of kings, and lightning strikes the highest mountains.
